title: Domain-truth fixtures (domain-truth.json)
$comment: Domain-SOUNDNESS fixtures for non-coding default-surface skills (road-to-domain-soundness Phase 1). DISTINCT from evals.json (behavioural output quality) and triggers.json (activation): a domain-truth case asserts the embedded domain heuristic is actually CORRECT off the forged TS/PHP stacks. Every case's answer key must be traceable to a CITED external method/standard — never the skill's own output (that validates nothing). A skill lacking this file is `unvalidated`; presence + a passing run makes it `validated`.

skill.description: Skill slug; must match the parent skill directory name.

domain.description: The non-coding domain whose ground truth this fixture checks.

_note.description: Optional free-text note (calibration / provenance status). Advisory.

cases.description: One or more domain-truth cases: a scenario + a domain-correct answer key with a SOURCED rationale.

id.description: Stable case slug, unique within this file.

scenario.description: The input scenario handed to the skill under test.

source.description: The CITED external method/standard the answer key is traceable to (a finance text, an IC framework, a named practice). A case whose key cannot cite an external basis is not a domain-truth case — it is rejected. NEVER the skill's own output.

check.description: How soundness is judged. Deterministic where the domain has a right number; rubric where it does not (the rubric criterion must name the cited practice, graded by a pinned judge, recorded as a known-limit — never a hidden LLM-judge).

expected.description: The computed-correct answer (e.g. a runway in months, an NPV) with the working shown in `rationale`.

tolerance.description: Absolute tolerance for a numeric expected value (0 = exact).

rationale.description: The working that derives `expected` from the cited method, so a maintainer without the domain can check the key against the source, not against the skill.

criterion.description: Pass criterion phrased as "matches <named practice>", graded by a pinned judge. NON-deterministic — recorded as a known-limit with a witness.
